new_foods.source: PROVISIONAL (nalt-names-10): Martinez Steele et al., J Nutr2023, Table1 Group1, "Natural, packaged, cut, chilled or frozen vegetables, fruits, potatoes, cassava, and other roots and tubers"; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10127522/ . The exact term root vegetables is not named: class-instance of the stated plain food category, supported independently by current USDA NALT Product12359, https://lod.nal.usda.gov/nalt/12359, checked2026-11-22, CC BY4.0 (identity and edible-food category, not NOVA). The same current paper explicitly includes fresh, dry or frozen fruits/vegetables and grinding/roasting in its Group1 definition; fungi are separately named in Table1. Bare food category only, no added substances. This does not grant placement to unspecified powders, extracts, isolates, preserved foods or oil-roasted products. Existing item-own form/composition guards remain. Not a strong marker. Current Table1 Group3 independently supports same-food preparations with culinary additions: "These are relatively simple products manufactured essentially with the addition of salt or sugar or other substances of common culinary use, such as oil or vinegar, to unprocessed or minimally processed foods." Salt/sugar/brine or explicit culinary additions use the existing item-own Group3 guard; unknown additions and insufficiently specified preserved products still abstain.
new_foods.inference_level: class-instance of named food category, not exact-named food

notes: Four new ingredient/category heads and five exact names, not four disjoint biological foods or a coverage percentage.
No plural of a held food is admitted to bypass its unresolved scope.
No jerky-vegetable synonym: the broad product page does not establish its composition or processing.

No hot-pepper, gherkin, squash-beverage, dewberry/blackberry, loganberry/boysenberry, pulse-form or botanical-bramble synonym is forced through. Those remaining candidates need separate sense/form review.

Initial green-leafy canonical with a shorter leafy-vegetables alias repeated the green modifier. The canonical is now the explicit NALT leafy-vegetables synonym; the preferred green-leafy phrase maps to it. Exact canonical and target normalization are independently tested.

Dried/dehydrated vegetables are held from this slice after affected-form controls: existing oil normalization and unsupported powder routes need separate review. Initial fungi tests also showed whole/pure-powder and powder-plus-sugar abstentions. The later wide controls rejected both fungi heads entirely.

Wide cross-ingredient controls rejected both new fungi heads: unsupported nested powders could answer under culinary-ingredient and 100%-powder parents. They are excluded rather than changing broad guards. Final slice has four category heads and five exact names only.
